title: No evidence for Z-shaped web scan pattern
statement:
No web eyetracking study we could find establishes a Z-shaped scan pattern; Z-pattern layouts are a practitioner heuristic borrowed from the print-era Gutenberg diagram for sparse pages, so treat them as a composition guideline and give priority to evidence-backed cues such as left-side attention, clear headings and aligned images.

Options:
- Z-composition as a heuristic: Z-shaped composition for a sparse page: logo left, CTA right in the header, hero visual on the diagonal, final CTA at the bottom right (heuristic, unverified) (fits: minimal, bold, promotional)
- Evidence-backed left alignment: Left-aligned headline and CTA in the hero, supported by NN/g findings on left-biased attention rather than a Z path (fits: professional, clear, trustworthy)
- Heading-led structure: Layer-cake structure with clear headings and chunked sections instead of a diagonal path (fits: editorial, organized, clear)
- Aligned rows, sparing zigzag: Aligned image-text rows, with zigzag only for short sequences of informative images (fits: clean, calm, practical)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general.
